rule: All resolved places remain selectable with a score; only independently audited settlements scoring 60 or more appear as town markers.

additions.name: Woodside (Largo)
additions.rationale: Woodside is retained as the hamlet west of New Gilston and is not confused with Woodside in Aberdeen or allowed to inherit Ceres, Peat Inn or Largo attractions.
additions.resolutionNote: Resolved to Woodside beside New Gilston in Fife; displayed with Largo qualifier to prevent ambiguity.

additions.name: New Gilston
additions.rationale: New Gilston is assessed on its own historic settlement fabric and community hall without borrowing neighbouring estates, scheduled cairns or destination restaurants.

additions.name: Wester Newburn
additions.rationale: Wester Newburn is a farm locality rather than a visitor village; Newburn churches, Largo Law and nearby accommodation remain outside its settlement score.

additions.name: Lundin Links
additions.rationale: Lundin Links is assessed independently through its beach-edge setting, scheduled standing stones, golf visitor offer, daytime coffee and routes that genuinely enter the village.

additions.name: Lower Largo
additions.rationale: Lower Largo is assessed on its harbour, beach, Alexander Selkirk associations, independent trails, café and practical facilities without inheriting Upper Largo or Leven.
additions.resolutionNote: The requested spelling is normalised to Lower Largo.

additions.name: Drumeldrie
additions.rationale: Drumeldrie keeps its strong Newburn church history in See, but that heritage alone does not make the hamlet a rounded visitor destination.
additions.resolutionNote: The requested spelling is normalised to the established Drumeldrie.

additions.name: Leven
additions.rationale: Leven receives a complete town-scale audit of its beach, parks, heritage railway, family activity, coffee-and-cake stops, trails and public facilities.
